title: rigscope — see your PC's hardware in detail
description: A desktop app for Linux and Windows that shows every RAM slot, the CPU, disks with SMART health, graphics, network, battery and sensors in one window.
hero_title: Your computer's hardware, slot by slot
hero_lead: Every RAM slot, the CPU, disks with their SMART health, graphics, network, battery and sensors, without opening a terminal. And the answer that usually starts the search: which RAM can I buy for this machine?
hero_note: Tested on real Windows 10 hardware. Not yet run on a real Linux machine: there it was built and tested in a container with synthetic hardware data. Reports from real Linux hardware are welcome.
shot_memory_alt: rigscope, the Memory section with the compatibility line and the slot table
f1_p: Every slot: maker, part number, size, rated and running speed, ranks, voltage. Empty slots and the board maximum, plus a compatibility line to paste into a shop search.
f2_p: Model, sockets, cores and threads, base and max clock, live clock per core, caches, microcode and instruction set extensions.
f3_p: NVMe, SATA, USB and virtual disks: model, capacity, SSD or HDD, firmware, serial and SMART health with warnings.
f4_p: Cards named from pci.ids, driver, PCIe link and video memory where the driver exposes it. Wi-Fi and Ethernet adapters with speed and state.
f5_p: Capacity, health derived from design capacity, cycles, live temperatures with limits and fan speeds.
f6_p: Copy a report as text or JSON with serial numbers, MAC addresses and the hostname masked, ready for a forum post.
shot_storage_alt: rigscope, the Storage section with SMART
priv_p1: Most details come from /proc and /sys as a normal user. The SMBIOS table (slot details) and SMART need root, so rigscope asks for your password in the system dialog (polkit) and reads them then.
priv_p2: Nothing of rigscope runs as root: pkexec starts the system shell with a fixed script that only prints the DMI table and the smartctl output. There is nothing to install, so it works from the AppImage too.
dl_deb: Ubuntu, Debian, Mint. Adds rigscope to the application menu.
dl_appimage: Any Linux x86_64. One file, no install.
dl_tar: Any Linux x86_64. Binary and licences.
dl_windows: Windows (x86_64, portable .exe). Windows 10 1809 or later; asks for administrator rights at each start; not code-signed (SmartScreen: More info, Run anyway).
dl_mac: macOS 11+, Apple silicon and Intel. Shows a demo machine; not notarized (right click, Open).
